questions.question: How do you detect a force push from git log data?
choices: Check if the commit hash is longer than usual
Check if a commit's parent doesn't match the previous commit by the same author
Check if the commit message contains 'force'
Check if the commit was made on a weekend
questions.explanation: A force push rewrites history by changing commit parents. If an author's new commit has a parent that doesn't match their last known commit hash, it means history was rewritten.

questions.question: What does a 'revert' in a commit message typically indicate?
choices: Some previously committed code was undone
questions.explanation: A revert commit undoes changes from a previous commit. While reverts are sometimes necessary, frequent reverts may indicate issues with code quality or review processes.

questions.question: Why must you filter out missing dates before sorting?
choices: JavaScript sort() throws on undefined values
undefined values sort to the end by default, giving wrong ranges
questions.explanation: Some log entries may not have a date field. Calling .sort() on an array with undefined values can produce unexpected results or errors. Filter(Boolean) removes falsy values first.
